previous_statement: Assume emptyset!=U proper-subset C has the stated reset, choose j in C minus U, set R:=U union \{j\}, epsilon_R:=W.L*epsilon, and t_2:=W.K2*epsilon. Because U and j lie in the same equivalence class and the structural and ledger inequalities give epsilon<=W.e_s2/W.K2, 0<=t_2<=W.e_s2 and W.r_reset, apply lem-maincb-stage2-call-envelope to obtain the explicit Stage-2 EXT raw-call datum in A_R with recorded target field epsilon_R and total defect at most C_s2^0*t_2; then lem-maincb-stage2-raw-extension supplies its literal map u_2:M_{|U|+1}->A_R, and lem-maincb-reset-constant-ledger records that same map as an extended D_*t_2-isomorphism with ||u_2(I)-u_{A_R}||<=D_*t_2 and eligibility for reset preservation.
new_statement: Assume emptyset!=U proper-subset C has the stated reset, choose j in C minus U, and set R:=U union {j}, epsilon_R:=W.L*epsilon, and t_2:=W.K2*epsilon. Since U and j lie in the same equivalence class, the Stage-2 call-envelope hypotheses hold; the direct aggregate Stage-2 producer conclusion in lem-maincb-reset-constant-ledger, with the structural scale bounds, supplies the literal map u_2:M_{|U|+1}->A_R as an extended D_*t_2-isomorphism satisfying ||u_2(I)-u_{A_R}||<=D_*t_2 and eligible for reset preservation. This conclusion is obtained without separately invoking lem-maincb-stage2-raw-extension.
